newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks down slightly by lunch, awaiting data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks down slightly by lunch, awaiting data.

text.p: Local retailers sold finance issues and took profits as they waited for key central bank economic indicators, especially on foreign reserves, to be released around 0800 GMT, brokers said.

"The market was a bit sluggish this morning as investors watched whether the country's foreign reserves would drop sharply or not after the central bank had spent money on defending the baht earlier," said a broker.
The composite SET index declined 1.34 points to 678.19 on 2.3 billion baht turnover by the lunch break.
Thai foreign reserves in May stood at $33.3 billion.
Investors were concerned that June foreign reserves would fall below $30 billion following weeks of a currency war waged by the authorities with baht speculators in May and June.

Touching on a decision by the exchange to postpone the introduction of the 30 percent daily trading limit on common shares originally planned for Friday, brokers said the decision would affect retailers who bought for speculative reasons earlier as they could only make smaller profits.
Nava Finance topped the active list, gaining 1.25 baht to 34. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
